claims.text: In-situ high-temperature X-ray diffraction under a controlled oxygen atmosphere enables real-time detection of transient oxide phases in nickel-based alloys.
Detecting transient oxide phases by HT-XRD captures high-temperature oxidation behavior.
In-situ HT-XRD can assess phase stability in nickel-based alloys during heating.
Heating a nickel-based alloy in oxygen causes oxidation reactions to initiate and progress.
Oxidation during heating leads to phase transformations.
Oxidation-induced phase transformations are directly observable as changes in HT-XRD diffraction patterns.
Emerging diffraction peaks indicate the formation of transient oxide phases.
Distinct diffraction peaks corresponding to new oxide phases will appear as temperature increases.
The evolution of oxide diffraction peaks correlates with oxidation onset and subsequent phase transformations.
Conventional room-temperature XRD does not capture phase changes in real time during oxidation.
HT-XRD sensitivity may be limited below the temperature at which observable oxide formation occurs.
The resolution of HT-XRD phase identification can vary with alloy composition and experimental setup.
The onset temperature for detecting transient oxide phases can vary.
Complementary techniques may be required to calibrate or validate HT-XRD phase identification.
Thermogravimetric mass-gain measurements can cross-validate oxidation inferred from HT-XRD.
